description: Note generator that adds one of two numbers to a running value at each clock and picks a note by counting the 1s in that value written in a chosen base

params.text: Sets the low part of addend A, 0 to 63
Sets the high part of addend A, 0 to 63, each step worth 64
Sets the low part of addend B, 0 to 63
Sets the high part of addend B, 0 to 63, each step worth 64
Sets the base the running value is written in before its 1s are counted, 1 to 10; at 1 the running value itself becomes the note index
Appends the scale in reverse, so the sequence turns round at the top instead of dropping back
Sets how many notes the scale runs to, 1 to 24, repeating the chosen notes an octave higher once they run out
Chooses when a note is played: 1 at every clock pulse, 2 only when the note differs from the one before, 3 only when it repeats the one before
Shifts the played note by -24 to 24 semitones, or by that many notes of the scale when the REL button is lit
Sets how often addend B is added in place of addend A, never at 0 and always at 1
Puts the running value back to the start value
Sets the low part of the starting value, 0 to 63; moving it reloads the running value from the start value
Sets the high part of the starting value, 0 to 63, each step worth 64; moving it reloads the running value from the start value
Adds that note to the scale or takes it out; the last remaining note cannot be switched off
Makes the offset count notes of the scale rather than semitones

inputs.text: Each rising edge adds one of the two addends to the running value and plays the note that follows from it
Adds to the offset knob at 1V per octave, a twelfth of a volt per semitone, the total held to -24 to 24 semitones
Adds a tenth of its voltage to the probability knob, so 10V alone always picks addend B
A rising edge above 1V puts the running value back to the start value

outputs.text: Rests at 10V and drops to 0V for 1ms at each note played
The pitch of the note being played, 1V per octave, limited to -5V to 5V

notes: A note is played only on a rising edge at the CLK input, so with nothing patched there the outputs never change
